A_target.statement:
In any [[Definition:Acceptable Programming System|acceptable programming language]], there exists a program $p$ whose output is its own source code:
:$\map {\operatorname {output} } p = \ulcorner p \urcorner$

B_source.statement:
Let $f$ be a [[Definition:Total Recursive Function|total computable function]] on program indices.
Then there exists $e$ such that $\phi_e = \phi_{\map f e}$.
This is [[Kleene's Recursion Theorem]].

substitutions.the computable transformation of program: the transformation sending a program to one that prints that program's source

derived.the fixed point equation on programs: a program whose behaviour is to output its own text
derived.the effectiveness of the construction: the quine can actually be written down, not merely shown to exist

object_map.reformulation: Express self-printing as invariance under the print-my-argument transformation, making the quine a fixed point.

validity_conditions: The transformation sending a source text to a program printing that text is total and computable, which is the hypothesis the recursion theorem requires.
The theorem gives a program computing the same function as its transform, which here means outputting its own source.
The proof is constructive, so the fixed point can be exhibited explicitly; this is why quines can be written in practice rather than only shown to exist.
proof_plan: Let $f$ be the map sending an index $e$ to the index of a program which ignores its input and prints $\ulcorner e \urcorner$.
$f$ is total and computable, so [[Kleene's Recursion Theorem]] applies.
